channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: Georgian Sailors Survive Iranian Attack On Ship Off Iraqi Coast
item.description: All 23 Georgian crew members aboard a Malta-flagged tanker struck by Iran of the Iraqi coast have been rescued, a relative of one of the sailors told RFE/RL's Georgian Service.

item.title: Oil Tankers Ablaze In Gulf After Iranian Drone Boat Attack
item.description: Two fuel tankers in the Persian Gulf were hit by Iranian attacks on March 12, authorities say. Iranian state television claimed at least one vessel was struck by a boat loaded with explosives. At least one person was killed in the attacks and 38 rescued, including 23 Georgian sailors.

item.title: Congress To Be Briefed As Probe Examines Iran School Strike, Sources Tell RFE/RL
item.description: A final assessment by US military officials of events surrounding a deadly missile strike on an Iranian girls' school will be shared with Congress in the coming days, sources told RFE/RL amid growing reports that the attack was likely launched by the United States.

item.title: Turkey, Central Asia Look To Slovakia To Get Russian Oligarch Usmanov Off EU Sanctions List
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Azerbaijan, and three Central Asian republics are, via Slovakia, pushing to get Russian-Uzbek oligarch Alisher Usmanov removed from the European Union’s sanctions list ahead of a15 March roll-over of the bloc’s extensive blacklist.

item.title: US-Israeli Bombing Of Iran's Energy Infrastructure Marks New Escalation In War
item.description: The United States and Israel have targeted economic and civilian infrastructure in Iran in recent days, a new escalation in the war, experts say.

item.title: Iran To Keep Strait Of Hormuz Closed, Supreme Leader Khamenei Says In First Public Comments
item.description: Iran must continue to keep a key Gulf shipping lane closed, ⁠Supreme ⁠Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in his first public comments since being named to succeed his late father, hours after several vessels were targeted in strikes as Tehran looks to choke off oil supplies from leaving the Middle East.

item.title: Iran's Navy Is Largely Gone. The Threat To The Strait Of Hormuz Is Not.
item.description: The US has sunk 60 Iranian navy vessels and destroyed most of Iran's conventional fleet. But the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed because Iran doesn't need a navy to keep ships out.

item.title: Israeli President Calls For 'Hitting Iran Hard' As Attacks Continue On Both Sides
item.description: The exchange of fire between Iran and Israel continued on March 12, with strikes hitting civilian sites in central Israel. Speaking to RFE/RL, Israeli President Isaac Herzog said his country aims to keep up the intense campaign to "remove [Iran's] capabilities" to wage war.

item.title: Investigation Highlights Iran's Growing Footprint In Georgia
item.description: Georgia’s State Security Service has launched an investigation into claims that Iran is expanding its influence in the country through Georgian Shi'ite communities, growing concerns about Tehran’s religious and political outreach in the South Caucasus country.

item.title: US Warplane Down, French Soldier Killed In Iraq As Iran War Effects Spread
item.description: A giant US refueling plane crashed in Iraq after an apparent midair collision, while a French soldier was killed in the country’s Kurdistan region as the 2-week-old US-Israeli war on Iran continued to spill over regional borders.
